candidates.title: PureDB IPv6 allow/deny IP rules are silently discarded, bypassing per-user deny lists
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/pure-pw.h:36-38
src/pure-pw.c:710-731
src/utils.c:59-79
src/log_puredb.c:412-441
src/log_puredb.c:225-232
candidates.reason: pure-pw writes IP-rule text verbatim into a ':'-delimited PureDB record and pure_strtok2 splits on every ':'. An IPv6 literal such as ::1/128 therefore produces empty allow/deny fields (the shifted fragment lands after the time field), and access_ip_check() treats the empty deny list as permitting access, so the configured per-user IPv6 deny rule is never enforced.

candidates.title: heap_buffer_overflow at src/coap_block.c:1879
candidates.label: UNKNOWN

candidates.reason: The unchecked marker write is real, but the reported default-UDP trigger is statically contradicted: the incoming request and the 4.08 response share the same PDU size limit and the mandatory Size1/RTag options leave no room for a PDU-filling token. src/coap_oscore.c:1856-1867 frees only associations and PDUs on failure, not the duplicated context
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Strix report: unauthenticated B.2 requests with fresh kid_context values accumulate permanently linked OSCORE contexts, causing unbounded memory growth.

candidates.title: pdu_408_build writes the payload marker without checking capacity
candidates.label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_block.c:1867-1880 writes the payload marker unconditionally after ignoring token and option add results
src/coap_pdu.c:439-446 permits an exact-fill token and src/coap_pdu.c:395-412 refuses further growth
src/coap_block.c:3542-3547 requires Size1 and RTag on Q-Block1 requests, reducing room for a PDU-filling token
src/coap_pdu.c:139 sets alloc_size=min(size, COAP_DEFAULT_MTU) while max_size can be larger, so transport/CSM sizing determines reachability
candidates.reason: The one-byte unchecked marker write is real, but the report itself calls it latent and the default-UDP path is blocked by the shared PDU limit plus mandatory Q-Block1 options. Whether a TCP/CSM or other configuration admits a PDU-filling token is a runtime/transport fact not settled by the snapshot.

candidates.title: Block1 reassembly can hand uninitialized heap bytes to the application
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_block.c:3604 derives the write offset from the current block.szx
src/coap_block.c:3693-3697 stores lg_srcv->szx but never rejects a later block with a different SZX
src/coap_block.c:4594-4596 allocates the body without zeroing; src/coap_str.c:42-46 zeroes only the header
src/coap_block.c:4050-4058 hands total_len bytes to the application even though only received segments were copied
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Strix report: a mid-transfer SZX increase creates a never-written gap in the reassembled body, which is then exposed to the application with the full total length.

candidates.title: OSCORE Appendix B.2 kid_context encoder writes past the 255-byte stack buffer and underflows its remaining-space counter
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore.c:221-231 shifts the write pointer by one but passes the unshifted rem_space and then can underflow it
src/oscore/oscore_cbor.c:104-118 copies bytes_len once the remaining counter equals bytes_len
src/oscore/oscore.c:247-254 the key-id bound check is bypassed after rem_space underflows to SIZE_MAX
src/coap_oscore.c:418 holds the 255-byte stack buffer; src/coap_oscore.c:541 invokes B.2 encoding
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: the B.2 CBOR wrapper under-accounts by one byte, allowing a one-byte stack write and then an unbounded key-id copy after the counter underflow.

candidates.title: WebSocket close path can overflow a 100-byte stack buffer with a partial frame
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_ws.c:697-707 checks the frame size only against the current call's datalen and leaves all_hdr_in set on a partial frame
src/coap_ws.c:762-764 requests data_size-data_ofs bytes from l_read on resumption without rebounding to the new datalen
src/coap_ws.c:900-914 drains with uint8_t buf[100] and calls coap_ws_read(session, buf, sizeof(buf))
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: a partial WebSocket frame plus close-drain re-entry with a 100-byte buffer lets the stale frame size drive an out-of-bounds stack write.

candidates.title: OSCORE external credential lookup can return a context with no recipient and crash the server
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore_context.c:371-396 returns tmp_ctx after freeing all recipients when none matches, leaving *recipient_ctx NULL
src/coap_oscore.c:1064-1068 passes rcp_ctx initialized to NULL into the lookup
src/coap_oscore.c:1146-1157 dereferences rcp_ctx->initial_state without checking rcp_ctx
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Strix report: an external multi-recipient credential set without the request KID yields a non-NULL context with a NULL recipient, which the request path dereferences before authentication.

candidates.title: Short OSCORE responses advance the replay window without rollback
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1370-1382 advances rcp_ctx->last_seq before AEAD verification on responses
src/coap_oscore.c:1482-1501 the short-ciphertext response branch omits oscore_roll_back_seq()
src/coap_oscore.c:1541-1551 the generic decrypt-failure path does roll back
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: an on-path attacker can advance the response replay window with a forged short high-PIV response, causing later genuine responses to be rejected.

candidates.title: Uri-Path-Abbrev fallback retransmit drops the request body
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_net.c:1801-1808 adds the payload to the old PDU and frees it, while new is sent without data
src/coap_pdu.c:271-281 duplication copies options but not payload
src/coap_block.c:5191-5196 demonstrates the correct target for the re-added body
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: the fallback retransmit attaches the request body to the discarded PDU, so the expanded request on the wire silently loses its payload.

candidates.title: coap_ws_close 用 100 字节栈缓冲复读未完成 WebSocket 帧
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_ws.c:697-707 is the only frame-size check and compares against the datalen of the header-parsing call
src/coap_ws.c:762-764 resumes with l_read(&data[data_ofs], data_size-data_ofs) without rebounding to the caller-supplied datalen
src/coap_ws.c:900-914 calls coap_ws_read(session, buf, sizeof(buf)) with uint8_t buf[100] during close drain
src/coap_ws.c:681 keeps all_hdr_in set for a partially received frame
candidates.reason: A partial frame leaves all_hdr_in set with data_size larger than the close-drain buffer. The resume path asks l_read for data_size-data_ofs bytes into the 100-byte stack buffer, giving a concrete attacker-controlled stack overwrite when WebSocket support and a WS endpoint are enabled and close timing is met.

candidates.title: Uri-Path-Abbrev 回退重传时载荷被加到旧 PDU 并随旧 PDU 释放
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_net.c:1801-1808 duplicates the request into new, then calls coap_add_data(pdu, ...) on the old PDU and frees that old PDU
src/coap_pdu.c:233-235 documents that coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd() copies only token and options, not data
src/coap_block.c:5191-5196 shows the correct pattern, adding the saved body to the new duplicate
candidates.reason: Once no_path_abbrev is set, the fallback retransmit adds the body to the PDU that is immediately deleted, so the transmitted duplicate carries no payload. This silently changes request integrity for body-bearing requests on sessions using Uri-Path-Abbrev.

candidates.title: 单字节 WebSocket Close 载荷读取未初始化字节
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_ws.c:720-729 enters the close branch when the received close-frame length is 1 and computes close_reason from data[0] and data[1]
src/coap_ws.c:729 reads data[1] even though only one byte was copied into the caller buffer
src/coap_ws.c:899-914 later sends close_reason back to the peer
candidates.reason: A 1-byte WebSocket Close payload makes the code read an uninitialized byte and echo it as part of the close reason. The defect is real but discloses only a single byte to the same peer; WebSocket support is required.

candidates.title: coap_rebuild_pdu_for_proxy 移除 Proxy-Uri 后使用旧指针
candidates.label: FP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:288-322 parses Proxy-Uri, removes the option, then uses uri.host/path/query to build new options
src/coap_uri.c:256,331,340 set uri fields to point into the Proxy-Uri option value inside the PDU buffer
src/coap_pdu.c:635-639 memmove stays within the same PDU allocation and only shrinks used_size
src/coap_oscore.c:296-322 uses lengths bounded by the original option value
candidates.reason: The stale pointers remain within the existing PDU allocation and removal only shifts bytes within that allocation; no out-of-bounds access follows. Any wrong target bytes come from the attacker's own Proxy-Uri/PDU, so this is a correctness issue without a security-relevant path.

candidates.title: 代理 Hop-Limit 缺省与端点比较问题
candidates.label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_pdu.c:887-895 inserts a default Hop-Limit of 255 when a Proxy-Uri or Proxy-Scheme option is added
src/coap_net.c:3976-3980 only validates Hop-Limit when present
src/coap_net.c:4094-4113 only decrements when hop_limit >= 0
src/coap_net.c:3954-3958 uses case-sensitive coap_string_equal for proxy endpoint matching
candidates.reason: The report is too vague to map to a concrete loop or amplification path. A default Hop-Limit insertion exists for library-generated proxy options, and the residual case-sensitivity/self-loop concern depends on a specific proxy deployment that cannot be resolved from the snapshot.

candidates.title: %2F 主机被解析为本地 AF_UNIX 目标
candidates.label: UNKNOWN
evidence: src/coap_uri.c:260-264 treats a %2F host prefix as a Unix-domain definition
src/coap_uri.c:474-484 coap_host_is_unix_domain() also accepts hosts beginning with '/'
src/coap_address.c:749-770 resolves such hosts via coap_address_set_unix_domain()
src/coap_proxy.c contains no guard rejecting Unix-domain targets for dynamic forwarding
candidates.reason: The %2F-to-Unix-socket parsing is explicit and intentional, and no proxy guard blocks it, but security impact depends on whether an exposed FWD_DYNAMIC proxy is deployed and whether local Unix sockets are sensitive. That runtime/deployment fact is not resolvable from the snapshot.

candidates.title: OSCORE Appendix B.2 kid_context 的 CBOR 包装缓冲区空间少算 1 字节
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore.c:221 writes through ptr=&option_buffer[offset+1] but passes rem_space unchanged
src/oscore/oscore.c:226-231 subtracts 1 after oscore_cbor_put_bytes(), which underflows when the CBOR header plus kid_context exactly fills rem_space
src/oscore/oscore_cbor.c:104-118 copies bytes_len when the remaining counter equals bytes_len, so the last byte lands at option_buffer[255]
src/coap_oscore.c:418 declares uint8_t oscore_option[255]; src/coap_oscore.c:541 enables B.2 encoding when b_2_step != COAP_OSCORE_B_2_NONE
src/coap_oscore.c:1209-1234 stores an attacker-influenced R2||ID1 value as id_context that is later encoded
candidates.reason: Appendix B.2 CBOR wrapping advertises one byte more than is available at the shifted pointer; an aligned kid_context writes index 255, underflows rem_space, and lets the following key-id copy run past the 255-byte stack array. Reachable when B.2 mode is enabled.

candidates.title: OSCORE 响应侧短密文路径未回滚重放窗口（拒绝服务）
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1370-1382 validates and advances rcp_ctx->last_seq before AEAD verification on the response path
src/coap_oscore.c:1482-1501 short-ciphertext response branch logs the failure and jumps to error without oscore_roll_back_seq()
src/coap_oscore.c:1541-1551 other decryption failure paths do call oscore_roll_back_seq()
src/oscore/oscore.c:434-478 records rollback state before advancing the window
candidates.reason: The response replay window is advanced before authentication, and the encrypt_len <= tag_len response branch omits the rollback present in adjacent failure paths. An on-path attacker who can forge a short high-PIV response matching the token can make later genuine responses look like replays.

candidates.title: Request payload silently dropped when retransmitting Uri-Path-Abbrev requests (coap_net.c)
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_net.c:1801-1808 adds the body to the old PDU and frees it instead of adding it to new
src/coap_pdu.c:233-235 states duplication copies only token and options, not data
src/coap_block.c:5191-5196 shows the intended add-to-new-PDU behavior
candidates.reason: Same root cause as the Mygoldmine report: the Uri-Path-Abbrev fallback builds a duplicate without payload and writes the payload to the discarded original PDU, silently dropping request bodies.

candidates.title: Unauthenticated memory exhaustion in OSCORE Appendix B.2 context handling
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_oscore.c:1109-1122 calls oscore_duplicate_ctx() for an unknown kid_context before AEAD verification
src/oscore/oscore_context.c:743-746 oscore_enter_context() links the duplicate into c_context->p_osc_ctx
src/coap_oscore.c:1856-1867 error/error_no_ack releases associations and PDUs but never unlinks or frees the duplicated context
src/oscore/oscore_context.c:996-1008 only frees an unattached context on recipient release
candidates.reason: Each unauthenticated B.2 request with a fresh kid_context leaves a duplicated security context linked to the CoAP context after decryption fails. Repetition grows the chain without bound when B.2 is enabled and a valid recipient KID is known.

candidates.title: NULL pointer dereference in OSCORE external credential lookup crashes the server
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/oscore/oscore_context.c:371-396 assigns *recipient_ctx only on a KID match, then still returns tmp_ctx with *recipient_ctx left NULL when a multi-recipient set has no match
src/coap_oscore.c:1064-1068 expects oscore_find_context() to fill rcp_ctx, initialized to NULL
src/coap_oscore.c:1146-1157 calls the setter and dereferences rcp_ctx->initial_state before AEAD verification
examples/coap-server.c:3196-3197 registers the external find handler via coap_oscore_register_external_handlers()
candidates.reason: With the documented external credential callback and a multi-recipient (or zero-recipient) credential set lacking the request KID, the lookup returns a non-NULL context but a NULL recipient, and the request path dereferences it before authentication.

candidates.title: Uninitialised heap memory disclosed through re-assembled Block1 body when the block size grows mid-transfer
candidates.label: TP
evidence: src/coap_block.c:3604 computes offset from the current request's block.szx
src/coap_block.c:3693-3697 records the transfer SZX in lg_srcv->szx but no later check compares block.szx to it
src/coap_block.c:4050-4058 hands pdu->body_data with body_length = lg_srcv->total_len to the application
src/coap_block.c:4594-4596 allocates with coap_new_binary(), and src/coap_str.c:42-46 zeroes only the union header, not the payload area
src/coap_block.c:4620-4624 copies only the current segment, leaving any gap uninitialized
candidates.reason: A client that increases SZX between Block1 blocks makes the next offset jump past received data; reassembly still marks the transfer complete and hands the application total_len bytes with an uninitialized heap gap. Requires server-side single-body/Q-Block reassembly.

candidates.title: TLS 1.3 server authentication bypass: `tlse.c:9324` / `tlse.c:9379` / `tlse.c:10085`
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:8613-8631 the TLS 1.3 client advances to connection_status=2 after ServerHello
tlse.c:9269-9329 Finished parsing validates only the HMAC
tlse.c:9376-9379 the client sets connection_status=0xFF after Finished
tlse.c:9985-9997 certificate verification is skipped when no certificate was received
candidates.reason: The unparsed Claude section matches the source: TLS 1.3 client completion does not require Certificate or CertificateVerify.

candidates.title: Remote heap corruption via zero-length signature BIT STRING: `tlse.c:4598` / `tlse.c:4602`
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11370 default parser branch is active without TLS_FULL_X509
tlse.c:11580-11590 zero-length signature BIT STRING calls tls_certificate_set_sign_key
tlse.c:4597-4602 val[0] is read and len becomes -1
tlse.c:4546-4553 the negative length reaches malloc and memcpy
candidates.reason: The unparsed Claude section corresponds to the same default-build ASN.1 BIT STRING underflow as the Mygoldmine and Strix records.

candidates.title: Overlapping DTLS fragments overflow the stack reassembly buffer
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:12524 the bounds check covers offset+fragment_length against data_length but not accumulated written
tlse.c:12543-12550 allocation uses data_length*sizeof(char*) while written grows by each fragment_length
tlse.c:12552-12554 pending fragments persist because written != len
tlse.c:9802 local_buffer is DTLS_MAX_FRAGMENT_SIZE+12 on the stack
tlse.c:9847 memcpy uses fragment->written without checking the destination capacity
candidates.reason: Same overlapping-fragment accounting bug as the Strix record; accumulated written bytes overflow the fixed stack reassembly buffer.

candidates.title: STUN USERNAME and REALM attributes overflow the credential key buffer
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:13085 char key[0x4CE]
tlse.c:13184 USERNAME allowed up to 513 bytes
tlse.c:13254 REALM allowed up to 763 bytes
tlse.c:13210 the realm copy has no remaining-capacity check
tlse.c:13240 HMAC verification happens after the copy
candidates.reason: Same pre-authentication STUN key overflow reported by the other tools.

candidates.title: Zero-length certificate BIT STRING underflows into an unbounded memcpy
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11370 the default parser branch is used without TLS_FULL_X509
tlse.c:11580-11590 a zero-length BIT STRING calls tls_certificate_set_sign_key
tlse.c:4597-4602 the setter reads val[0] and decrements len to -1
tlse.c:4546-4553 set_copy allocates malloc(len+1) and memcpy's the negative length
candidates.reason: Same default-build ASN.1 BIT STRING underflow reported by the other tools.

candidates.title: tls_import_context reads mac_length without a preceding bounds check, allowing a one-byte out-of-bounds read
candidates.label: UNKNOWN
evidence: tlse.c:12812 key_lengths = buffer[buf_pos++]
tlse.c:12813-12815 TLS_IMPORT_CHECK_SIZE allows key_lengths to end exactly at buf_len, leaving buf_pos == buf_len
tlse.c:12858 mac_length = buffer[buf_pos++] then reads buffer[buf_len]
examples/tlshelloworld.c:190 is the only in-repo caller and imports its own exported buffer
candidates.reason: The missing check is real and yields a 1-byte over-read on a truncated import buffer, but exploitation depends on a host importing untrusted serialized state; no leak or write is shown and the in-repo caller self-imports.

candidates.title: tls_import_context CBC branch uses uninitialized stack IV bytes
candidates.label: FP
evidence: tlse.c:12768-12769 local_iv and remote_iv are fixed 16-byte arrays
tlse.c:12798-12810 iv_len is bounded by TLS_AES_IV_LENGTH and only that many bytes are copied
tlse.c:12851 the arrays are passed to _private_tls_crypto_create
libtomcrypt.c:33364 cbc_start copies the cipher block length from the IV
candidates.reason: Only stack bytes beyond iv_len are uninitialized; the arrays are not overflowed and a caller that supplies the imported buffer already controls the session keys. No security-relevant impact is demonstrated, making this a robustness issue.

candidates.title: TLS_REEXPORTABLE import path memcpy's into a TLS_MALLOC result without a NULL check
candidates.label: UNKNOWN
evidence: tlse.c:12816 #ifdef TLS_REEXPORTABLE
tlse.c:12818-12819 TLS_MALLOC followed by memcpy with no NULL check
CMakeLists.txt and tlse.h do not define TLS_REEXPORTABLE, so the default build omits this branch
candidates.reason: The defect exists only in an opt-in TLS_REEXPORTABLE build and additionally requires allocation failure; the default frozen build does not compile the path.

candidates.title: tls_parse_verify_request reads buf[13] past the DTLS HelloVerifyRequest buffer when its body is shorter than 3 bytes
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:7881-7886 res=11 and CHECK_SIZE(bytes_to_follow, buf_len - res) only proves L <= buf_len-11
tlse.c:7888-7889 res += 2 then len = buf[res] reads buf[13] with no remaining-length check
tlse.c:9953 case 0x03 passes the HelloVerifyRequest to tls_parse_verify_request for DTLS clients
tlse.c:9828-9830 payload_size is L+11 for DTLS
candidates.reason: A DTLS client role accepts a HelloVerifyRequest body of 0-2 bytes and reads buf[13], one to three bytes past the record's message buffer, before rejecting the record.

candidates.title: tls_stun_parse copies attacker-controlled REALM into fixed stack buffer key[0x4CE] before MESSAGE-INTEGRITY verification, causing a stack out-of-bounds write
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:13085 char key[0x4CE] (1230 bytes)
tlse.c:13184 USERNAME attr_len is allowed up to 513
tlse.c:13254 REALM attr_len is allowed up to 763
tlse.c:13210 memcpy(ptr, realm, realm_len) starts at key+username_len+1 with no remaining-capacity check
tlse.c:13240 MESSAGE-INTEGRITY memcmp happens after the realm copy
tlse.c:14006 tls_peerconnection_iterate forwards attacker datagrams to tls_stun_parse
candidates.reason: 513+1+763 exceeds the 1230-byte key, so an unauthenticated STUN binding request overflows the stack before the HMAC check.

candidates.title: Zero-length BIT STRING in the default ASN.1 parsing branch underflows len to -1 in tls_certificate_set_sign_key, making tls_certificate_set_copy perform a SIZE_MAX memcpy heap out-of-bounds write
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11308 and tlse.c:11370 select the default _private_asn1_parse branch when TLS_FULL_X509 is not defined; CMakeLists.txt defines no such macro
tlse.c:11482 length==0 takes the primitive branch
tlse.c:11580-11590 a level-2 idx-3 BIT STRING calls tls_certificate_set_sign_key(cert, &buffer[pos], 0)
tlse.c:4597-4602 set_sign_key reads val[0] and decrements len to -1 when the following byte is zero
tlse.c:4546-4553 set_copy treats -1 as non-zero, calls malloc(len+1)=malloc(0), then memcpy with SIZE_MAX
tlse.c:8702 tls_parse_certificate reaches asn1_parse on peer Certificate data before verification
candidates.reason: Default-build DER parser passes a zero-length signature BIT STRING to a setter that underflows len to -1 and then performs an unbounded memcpy on glibc.

candidates.title: Zero-length BIT STRING in X.509 DER causes memcpy with size -1 (remote crash) in TLSe
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11370 default parser branch is compiled without TLS_FULL_X509
tlse.c:11580-11590 zero-length level-2 idx-3 BIT STRING reaches tls_certificate_set_sign_key
tlse.c:4597-4602 val[0] read and len-- produce -1
tlse.c:4546-4553 malloc(len+1) and memcpy with the negative length
tlse.c:8702 certificate parsing happens before the verification callback
candidates.reason: Same default-build ASN.1 underflow as the Mygoldmine record: a crafted certificate reaches an unbounded memcpy before verification.

candidates.title: Stack buffer overflow in tls_stun_parse() key construction (WebRTC/STUN, pre-auth)
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:13085 char key[0x4CE]
tlse.c:13184 USERNAME may be 513 bytes
tlse.c:13254 REALM may be 763 bytes
tlse.c:13210 realm memcpy lacks a capacity check
tlse.c:13240 HMAC comparison is after the copy
tlse.c:14006 tls_peerconnection_iterate is the pre-auth entrypoint
candidates.reason: Same pre-authentication STUN credential-key stack overflow as the Mygoldmine record.

candidates.title: TLS 1.3 client accepts Finished without CertificateVerify, enabling certificate impersonation
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:8613-8631 the client sets connection_status=2 after ServerHello key_share
tlse.c:9269-9329 tls_parse_finished verifies only the Finished HMAC
tlse.c:9376-9379 the TLS 1.3 client sets connection_status=0xFF after Finished
tlse.c:9985-9997 the certificate callback runs only if certificates_count is non-zero
candidates.reason: The TLS 1.3 client does not require Certificate or CertificateVerify, so an active server that controls the key share and computes Finished is accepted without proving possession of the certificate key.

candidates.title: DTLS cookie is not bound to the client source address, allowing replay to spoofed peers and amplification
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:7775-7804 cookie is HMAC-SHA256(dtls_secret, remote_random) with no address input
tlse.c:8219 remote_random is copied from the incoming ClientHello
tlse.c:8255-8266 a fresh context builds the cookie from the same replayed random and accepts it
tlse.c:7816-7817 tls_build_verify_request uses the same process-secret cookie
candidates.reason: The DTLS cookie depends only on a process-wide secret and attacker-chosen client_random, so a cookie obtained from one source is accepted from other source addresses and fresh contexts.

candidates.title: Zero-length CBC record triggers 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read (pt[-1]) in tls_parse_message
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:10489-10505 the CBC decryption path allocates pt=malloc(length) without rejecting length 0
libtomcrypt.c:33004-33005 cbc_decrypt returns success for len 0
tlse.c:10715 padding_byte = pt[length - 1] reads pt[-1] when length == 0
tlse.c:10494 the length>=8 guard applies only to AEAD records
candidates.reason: After a CBC cipher is installed, a zero-length record causes malloc(0) and a read of pt[-1]; reachable by a remote peer but with limited standalone impact.

candidates.title: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow in DTLS fragmented handshake reassembly (TLSe)
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:12524 only checks fragment_offset+fragment_length <= data_length
tlse.c:12543-12550 allocates data_length*sizeof(char*) but increments written by fragment_length without a data_length bound
tlse.c:12552 written != len keeps the fragment pending even after written exceeds len
tlse.c:9802 local_buffer is DTLS_MAX_FRAGMENT_SIZE+12 bytes on the stack
tlse.c:9832 and tlse.c:9847 use written as the memcpy length into local_buffer
candidates.reason: Overlapping DTLS fragments accumulate written far beyond data_length; a later non-fragmented record copies written bytes into the fixed stack buffer, overflowing it pre-authentication.

candidates.title: Chain validation ignores basicConstraints and keyUsage: a non-CA certificate can issue certificates that TLSe reports as verified
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11076-11184 signature verification never inspects basicConstraints or keyUsage
tlse.c:11212-11238 tls_certificate_chain_is_valid checks dates and signatures only
tlse.c:11250-11305 tls_certificate_chain_is_valid_root checks issuer name, dates, and signature only
candidates.reason: A certificate marked CA:FALSE, or whose keyUsage omits keyCertSign, is accepted as an issuer whenever its signature verifies to a loaded trust anchor.

candidates.title: Out-of-bounds write in tls_certificate_to_string(): negative size passed to snprintf once the rendered peer certificate exceeds the caller's buffer
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:4612-4623 res accumulates snprintf return values and the next call uses len - res
tlse.c:4716-4719 and tlse.c:4750-4751 repeat the same pattern for key and signature output
no check requires res < len before buffer + res and len - res are used
candidates.reason: Once the rendered certificate exceeds the caller's len, len-res becomes negative and is converted to size_t, so snprintf writes past the caller's buffer with attacker-influenced certificate fields.

candidates.title: DTLS short handshake record causes out-of-bounds read of the fragment header in tls_consume_stream
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:12498 length is the record length field plus the 13-byte DTLS header
tlse.c:12508 the only guard is length > 13
tlse.c:12512-12516 twelve fragment-header bytes are read from buffer+13 without checking that the record carries them
candidates.reason: A DTLS handshake record with 1-11 payload bytes passes length > 13 and reads up to 11 bytes past the record/allocation while filling fragment bookkeeping fields.

candidates.title: Stale public-key/signature length after the key is cleared leads to a NULL pointer dereference in tls_certificate_to_string()
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:4581-4588 tls_certificate_set_key frees the old key through set_copy but updates pk_len only when the new pointer is non-NULL
tlse.c:4546-4557 tls_certificate_set_copy sets *member=NULL when len is zero
tlse.c:11580-11593 the parser can invoke set_key again with a zero-length BIT STRING at the pk_id path
tlse.c:4718-4719 tls_certificate_to_string iterates pk_len and dereferences cert->pk
candidates.reason: A certificate that sets the key twice, the second time empty, leaves pk NULL with a stale non-zero pk_len; rendering the certificate then dereferences NULL.

candidates.title: Client-certificate authentication is not enforced: handshake completes without a client certificate and tls_client_verified() returns true for an untrusted self-signed certificate
candidates.label: UNKNOWN
evidence: tlse.c:9991-9993 empty client certificates are explicitly permitted
tlse.c:9995-9996 the verification callback runs only when certificates_count is non-zero
tlse.c:10085-10108 Finished completes the handshake even when no client certificate was processed
tlse.c:12980-12984 tls_client_verified reports only the client_verified flag
candidates.reason: The source permits empty client certificates and delegates trust validation to the optional application callback; whether this bypasses authentication depends on application gating and callback installation, which cannot be resolved from the snapshot.

candidates.title: No DTLS anti-replay window: captured application-data records are re-delivered to the application indefinitely
candidates.label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:10787-10791 remote_sequence_number is overwritten from each received DTLS record
tlse.c:10554-10557 AEAD nonce and AAD are derived from the record's own epoch/sequence
no replay window or highest-sequence comparison exists in the DTLS receive path
candidates.reason: The DTLS record layer keeps no anti-replay state, so a captured record remains cryptographically valid and is delivered to the application again arbitrarily late.
